title: The Gysin class of a virtual normal sheaf of rank r caps the fundamental class of a Cohen-Macaulay situation to the fundamental class of the intersection
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a virtual normal sheaf N of a closed subscheme Z of X, a morphism Y -> X locally of finite type, and integers r, n, the lemma asserts that under four hypotheses - N locally free of rank r, every component of Y of dimension n, dim(Z x_X Y) <= n - r, and Cohen-Macaulayness of O_{Y,xi} at every point xi of Z x_X Y of dimension n - r - the Gysin class c(Z -> X, N) caps [Y]_n to [Z x_X Y]_{n-r} (statement lines 12127-12142). The proof reduces the global statement to a local one: since the target has dimension at most n - r its Chow group is freely generated by the components W of dimension n - r, so it suffices to work at the generic point xi of such a W (proof lines 12145-12151). There, dim(O_{Y,xi}) = r by the dimension hypothesis and, because N has rank r and its dual surjects onto the conormal sheaf, the ideal of Z is locally cut out by r equations; combined with Cohen-Macaulayness this makes I_xi generated by a regular sequence, which spreads to an open neighbourhood V of xi (proof lines 12152-12165). On V the excess normal sheaf vanishes, so the fundamental-class lemma applies and gives the required identity (proof lines 12166-12170). Turning the four hypotheses into a regular sequence at the generic point of each top dimensional component is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
